second_order: coordinating pictures from a starting pixel
theme_note: Participants turn a desired image into shared work by naming a starting point, asking for pixel-by-pixel help, handing work on, and moving to the next picture.

second_order: proposing more pictures and words for the canvas
theme_note: Participants put forward alternative characters, house sigils, slogans, or replacement targets; later proposals vary in whether they meet opposition or receive any outcome.

second_order: asking how the canvas drawing works
theme_note: This question seeks the practical meaning of the first drawing call and belongs with no other code closely enough to merge.

second_order: finding something else at the intended place
theme_note: Participants report what they encounter at a target rather than claiming to have built it; the observed marks vary from dat boi to a disputed Hodor reading.

second_order: requesting a fake April Fools leak
theme_note: The surviving title asks for a separate subreddit prank and has no completed answer, so it remains a single-code practice.

second_order: running the Funko sellout joke and giveaway
theme_note: Moderators establish and extend the claim that the room sold out to Funko, change what members are invited to post, tease and run a real giveaway, and close both activities.

second_order: playing along with and reacting to the Funko sellout
theme_note: Members recognize, praise, question, extend, solve problems inside, or reject the sellout fiction; the reactions vary without becoming moderator-run staging.

second_order: sharing Game of Bones again and again
theme_note: Many posters repeatedly submit the same or closely named Alt Shift X parody; the practice varies mainly in title wording, tags, deletion, and repost status.

second_order: arguing whether April Fools belongs in the title
theme_note: A poster is asked to hide the joke label and answers that the label is misleading rather than a spoiler; this is a labeling dispute, not another share.

second_order: calling for the subreddit to join r/place
theme_note: The removed-body post preserves a general participation call but no target, plan, or human uptake, so it stands alone.

second_order: reporting the pictures taking shape and finishing
theme_note: Builders report placed pieces, near-completion, completion, and success; these are status claims during the work rather than later praise for it.

second_order: correcting pixels to match the reference
theme_note: Participants shift focus, check colours, update diagrams, resist unwanted whitening, and later resolve placement errors by returning to the reference.

second_order: negotiating borders, space, and mutual help
theme_note: Neighbors and builders work out crossings, borders, portals, land, protection, and reciprocal upkeep; some negotiation stays on Reddit while part moves to Discord.
Participants choose maintenance over expansion, answer perceived threats, clear interference, and later guard the pictures; the threats and intensity vary.

second_order: celebrating and mourning the sigil work
theme_note: Participants applaud, toast, praise, joke about, take pride in, or mourn the work once it is visible or the canvas closes.

second_order: joking and trading insults around a Hodor find
theme_note: Before the lettering's origin is contested, commenters pun on the apparent name, attack a removed commenter, and ask why the room has not made something larger.
Contributors claim or apologize for changing the word while r/hoodr participants warn, correct, explain, and supply evidence that HOODR was intended.

second_order: calling for help and updates in other rooms
theme_note: Participants cross-post, request updates elsewhere, ask for a Discord, or point to a dedicated subreddit so work can travel beyond the thread.

second_order: channeling event posts through subreddit rules
theme_note: Human and automatic moderators redirect r/place talk to a sticky or remove proposals for missing spoiler tags; the practice governs where event talk can appear rather than deciding the canvas target.
